title: Exact colimit-preserving evaluation at an affine weakly contractible object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site, and let $W\to X$ be an affine site object which is weakly contractible: every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets induces a surjection $F(W)\to G(W)$. Then evaluation $\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R(W))$, $M\mapsto M(W)$, on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exact and preserves all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In particular, for every small filtered diagram $(M_i)$, its canonical comparison $\varinjlim_i M_i(W)\to(\varinjlim_i M_i)(W)$ is an isomorphism, natural in diagrams.

source.place: Tag 0946, label lemma-w-contractible, (1), module version using exact forgetful functor (03DA); Tag 0935, label lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact, (2). Exactness and preservation of direct sums imply preservation of all colimits by their cokernel presentation.

proof.text: Let $a:A\to B$ be an epimorphism of module sheaves. By the cokernel description, the presheaf $Q(V)=B(V)/a(A(V))$ has zero sheafification. Underlying-set sheafification and local equality therefore show that every $b\in B(V)$ locally belongs to $a(A)$. The underlying map of sheaves of sets is an epimorphism: if two maps out of $B$ agree after $a$, local lifts make them agree on a cover for every section of $B$, and separatedness makes them agree globally. This verifies the set-sheaf epimorphism hypothesis needed to use weak contractibility, rather than assuming module epimorphisms are sectionwise surjective.

Weak contractibility of $W$ now makes $A(W)\to B(W)$ surjective for each module epimorphism. Evaluation is additive and preserves kernels by sectionwise limits. For any $a:A\to B$, factor it as $A\twoheadrightarrow I\hookrightarrow B$, where $I=\ker(B\to\operatorname{coker}a)$. Applying the just-proved surjectivity to $A\twoheadrightarrow I$ and $B\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{coker}a$, and sectionwise kernels to both inclusions, gives $\operatorname{coker}(a(W))=(\operatorname{coker}a)(W)$. The same argument applied to a short exact sequence gives exactness of evaluation in $R(W)$-modules.

Let $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ be any small family and put $P(V)=\bigoplus_i M_i(V)$. Its sheafification is the sheaf coproduct, by the sectionwise-colimit description. For $s\in P^\#(W)$, underlying-set sheafification and local representation give a covering $V_a\to W$ and representatives $p_a\in P(V_a)$. By the covering definition on the pro-etale site, since $W$ itself is affine, choose finitely many affine opens $T_b\subset V_{a(b)}$ whose maps form a covering of $W$. Restrict the representatives to these $T_b$. Their supports have finite union $E\subset I$. This is the only use of affineness: a finite refinement exists even if the original covering is infinite.

source.place: Tag 0935 (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact), (2), expanded using the fpqc covering definition

proof.text: For each $i\in E$, the $i$-coordinates of these representatives agree on $T_b\times_W T_c$: their images in $P^\#$ agree there, so local equality after sheafification makes the coordinates locally equal, and separatedness of $M_i$ makes them equal on the overlap. Glue them to $m_i\in M_i(W)$. The finitely supported tuple $(m_i)$ maps to $s$, since this holds over every $T_b$. Conversely, if a finitely supported tuple maps to zero in $P^\#(W)$, local equality makes every coordinate locally zero, hence zero by separatedness. Thus the canonical $R(W)$-linear comparison $\bigoplus_i M_i(W)\to(\bigoplus_i M_i)(W)$ is bijective. For $I=\varnothing$ the source and target are zero, by the same argument.

For any small diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ form $B=\bigoplus_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}D(j)$ and $A=\bigoplus_{\alpha:j\to k}D(j)$. Define $d:A\to B$ on the $\alpha$-summand by the inclusion of $D(j)$ minus the inclusion of $D(k)$ composed with $D(\alpha)$. Maps from $B$ annihilating $d$ are exactly families $u_j:D(j)\to N$ satisfying $u_j=u_kD(\alpha)$, so $\operatorname{coker}d$ with its inclusions is the colimit, by its universal property. Both sums are small in the stipulated universes. Applying the direct-sum and cokernel comparisons proved above gives exactly the same presentation in $R(W)$-modules, hence the canonical colimit comparison is an isomorphism for every small $J$. This argument also covers the empty category.

The comparisons just obtained commute with each diagram-object inclusion by construction. For a natural transformation $D\to D\prime$, both composites in the comparison square therefore have equal composites with every inclusion $D(j)(W)$; the colimit universal property makes them equal. This proves naturality in diagrams. Specializing the arbitrary small indexing category to a filtered one gives the stated filtered-colimit comparison without additional hypotheses.
